brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 has full base at (0,0,0) and (1,0,0); level 1 has full base at (0,0,1) stacked on the first, so the tower spans two storeys.

requirements.requirement: The tower has at least two drawers.
requirements.evidence: Two notch drawer frames at level 0: notch:0#0,1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) and notch:0#1,-1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf), each filling the empty position between the two touching level-0 bases. check_build meshClash clear. Caveat: the drawers are notch-type frames, not the half-base drawer style, which was not offered here.

requirements.requirement: The build stays modest in size (under about 40 parts).
requirements.evidence: 6 nodes total: 3 pieces, 1 snap, 2 notch drawers.

finish.summary: Built a small two-storey storage tower: three hex bases (two on the ground level, one stacked above the first), with two notch drawer frames filling the open positions beside the ground-level bases. check_build reports no rule errors and a clear mesh check; only an info note about possible caps on open faces. The upper storey has no drawers or bins yet, and nothing has been filled or dressed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
